parsed.explanation: High Risk, driven by state-directed exposure rather than the sexuality statute alone. Police use Sections 365/365A as a lever for harassment, extortion and moral policing, and forced anal and vaginal examinations, widely condemned as torture, are documented. Police ignore complaints from LGBTQ victims, and the national police are named as the foremost perpetrators, so there is little effective recourse. Prison placement defaults to birth sex with no statutory rule and no dedicated transgender housing; a discretionary, medicalised exception applies, and the state has resisted gender-based placement. Care access is hostile, with reported ridicule and avoidance. Offsetting positives are a head-of-state statement, majority opposition to punishing LGBT people, a 2016 gender-recognition circular and political support. These are resident-facing or unevidenced for visitors and do not offset the custody and police exposures. Visitor-specific prosecution data is stale (2012), and the visitor passport and border treatment are undocumented, so those are open questions rather than established exposures.
